PC: Obtains a focused history from the patient, family, EMS or referring health care providers.
Initiates monitoring as appropriate for each scenario including pulse oximetry, blood pressure, and cardiac monitoring.
Assesses patient’s oxygenation status and places patient on supplemental oxygen in response to low oxygen saturation.
MK: Lists findings indicative of respiratory failure (increased/decreased respiratory rate, worsening hypoxia, mottling, bradycardia, thready pulses, altered mental status).
Lists the history and physical exam findings in upper airway obstruction.
Differentiates upper airway from lower airway pathology as a cause of respiratory distress.
Lists the appropriate pharmacologic therapy for anaphylaxis.
Lists the most common causes of airway obstruction.
ICS: Actively participates as a team member and is respectful of other team members and their input.
